name: Shang
place: the Yellow River plain, with its last capital at Yin (Anyang)
desc: The first Chinese dynasty that wrote: its kings asked their ancestors every question by cracking bones and turtle shells and carving the answers beside the cracks. They cast bronze cauldrons weighing nearly a tonne, rode chariots, and counted wealth in cowrie shells.
source: Oracle bones, first recognised in 1899; excavations at Yinxu, Anyang (from 1928), including the intact tomb of Fu Hao (1976)

devout: cracked a turtle shell and read that the harvest would be good
belligerent: drove the king's chariot in the hunt by the river
cautious: poured the bronze for a cauldron so big that it took a hundred men

inventions.name: Oracle Bones
inventions.source: Over 150,000 inscribed ox shoulder blades and turtle plastrons from Anyang, the oldest body of Chinese writing
inventions.desc: Hot bronze pressed to a prepared shell until it cracks; the diviner reads the crack and carves the question and answer: more lore, rites bring 10% more devotion.
inventions.hint: Needs the Tribe & Agrarian Era, and long rites.

inventions.name: The Great Cauldron
inventions.source: The Houmuwu ding (832 kg), cast for a queen mother, is the heaviest ancient Chinese bronze
inventions.desc: A four-legged bronze cauldron as heavy as ten oxen, for the meat offered to the ancestors: rites bring 15% more devotion, +2 mood.

inventions.name: War Chariots
inventions.source: Chariots with many-spoked wheels appear suddenly at Anyang around 1200 BCE, buried with their horses
inventions.desc: Two horses, a driver, an archer and a halberdier on a car of many spokes: +2 attack, everyone travels 3% faster.
inventions.hint: Needs Beast Domestication and Bronze Metallurgy.

inventions.name: Cowrie Shells
inventions.source: Cowries from the southern seas were treasured and given as rewards by Shang kings; the character for 'wealth' is drawn with a shell
inventions.desc: Little shells from the far sea, strung in tens and given as rewards: +2 mood, the stores hold 10 more.
inventions.hint: Comes from leading others and from travel.

foods.name: Wine for the Ancestors
foods.source: Shang tombs are full of bronze wine vessels; the Zhou later blamed the Shang's fall on drink
foods.desc: Millet wine poured from bronze vessels at every feast and rite: +3 mood, rites bring 5% more devotion.

foods.name: Yi Yin's Broth
foods.source: Lüshi Chunqiu, 'The Root of Flavour': the cook Yi Yin explained ruling by the art of blending tastes
foods.desc: A broth balanced in sour, sweet, bitter, hot and salty, as a cook would balance a kingdom: hunger grows 10% slower, +1 mood.
foods.hint: Needs pottery, and many hours at the hearth.

finds.name: River Turtles
finds.desc: Turtles of the river shallows; their under-shells are the best for divination. Once known, a little more lore.

finds.name: Mulberry Grove
finds.desc: Mulberry trees for fruit and for the silkworms. Once known, silk makes the cold bite 5% less.

people.name: Ke
people.source: Named after Que, one of the busiest diviners on the oracle bones of King Wu Ding
people.desc: He has cracked a thousand bones and carved every answer.
memory: asked the bones whether it would rain, and it rained

people.name: Gong
people.desc: He runs a foundry where a hundred people pour bronze at once.
memory: cast a ding with a face on each side that seemed to watch the room

people.name: Pangeng
people.source: Book of Documents, 'Pangeng'; the move to Yin around 1300 BCE
people.desc: The king who moved the capital to Yin over the people's complaints, and made three speeches to persuade them.

people.name: Yi Yin
people.source: Mencius; Lüshi Chunqiu; he is honoured as a high ancestor on the oracle bones
people.desc: A cook who became chief minister to Tang, the founder of Shang, and is said to have once sent a king into exile until he mended his ways.

people.name: Hai
people.text: a trader with strings of shining cowrie shells from the warm southern sea, who has walked for half a year.
memory: walked from the coast where the cowries wash up to the king's city
people.desc: A trader of the kind who brought cowries north to Shang.

people.name: Fu Hao
people.label: Fu Hao, General and Queen
people.desc: A queen who leads thirteen thousand into battle and performs the rites herself. Combat 8, Lore 5.

people.name: Wu Ding
people.label: Wu Ding the Great King
people.desc: The king of the oracle bones, who asks the ancestors about everything. Lore 7, Combat 6.

people.name: Tang
people.label: Tang the Victorious
people.desc: He overthrows a tyrant and offers himself for rain. Lore 6, Combat 6.

events.title: Ask the Ancestors
events.source: Oracle bone inscriptions ask about war, hunts, harvests, rain, childbirth and toothache, often as a pair: 'will it...?' / 'will it not...?'
events.text: Raiders have been seen to the west. The chief has the diviner crack a shell: 'If we attack, will the ancestors help us?' The crack runs long and straight.

options.label: Attack, as the bones say

do.remember: attacked when the bones said yes, and won

options.result: The raid is a success. The diviner carves a note beside the crack: it was so.

options.label: Ask again, the other way
options.result: 'Will the ancestors NOT help us?' The second crack is crooked. The chief waits, and the raiders move on.

events.title: Move the Capital
events.source: Book of Documents, 'Pangeng': the people did not want to move, and the king spoke to them three times
events.text: The river has flooded the town again. The chief wants to move everyone to higher ground across the river, but the people do not want to leave their homes.

options.label: Persuade them and move
options.result: Three speeches later, the people pack up. The new town never floods.

options.label: Stay and raise the dykes
options.result: The dykes go up a little higher.

events.title: A Pool of Wine
events.source: Records of the Grand Historian: the last Shang king made a pool of wine and a forest of hanging meat, and lost the mandate
events.text: The chief proposes a feast without end: a pool filled with wine, meat hanging from the trees, music day and night. The elders frown.

options.label: Hold the great feast
options.result: For a week no one works. Afterwards, people whisper that heaven has turned its face away.

options.label: Feast in moderation
options.result: One good night, and back to the fields.

tales.name: The Dark Bird
tales.source: Book of Songs, 'Xuan Niao'; Records of the Grand Historian
tales.text: Heaven commanded the dark bird to come down and give birth to Shang. Jiandi was bathing with her sisters when a swallow dropped an egg; she swallowed it, and bore Xie, the ancestor of the Shang kings.

tales.name: Tang Prays at the Mulberry Grove
tales.text: For five years no rain fell. King Tang cut his hair and nails, went to the mulberry grove and offered himself in place of his people: 'If I have done wrong, do not punish the people for it.' Before he had finished speaking, the rain came.

tales.name: The Cook Who Taught a King
tales.text: When King Tang asked how to rule, his cook answered with a recipe: the art lies in water and fire, in sour and sweet, bitter, hot and salt, in what comes first and what comes later. A kingdom is like a stew: too much of any one thing spoils it.

tales.name: The Feast of the Ten Days
tales.source: The Shang ritual calendar, with offerings to each ancestor on his or her day of the ten-day week
tales.text: Each ancestor has a day of the ten-day week: Day Jia, Day Yi, Day Bing. On the feast all ten are honoured together, the great cauldrons are filled, and the living eat with the dead.
tales.moral: the dead are part of the family
